key_insight: Foundational MLIPs with latent-feature delta-learning can correct DFT formation energies toward experimental accuracy, outperforming conventional GGA-level predictions without extra DFT runs.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, reproducible route to better thermodynamic screening of candidate materials, improving stability ranking for computational materials discovery.
method: Compare MC3D formation energies against OQMD, Materials Project, and experimental enthalpies
Use PET-OMATPES r2SCAN-trained foundational MLIP predictions to reduce DFT-to-experiment error
Train delta-learning models on latent MLIP features to further refine formation energies and phase stability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MLIP-based correction reduces mean absolute error by more than 40% relative to GGA, and the latent-feature delta-learning model lowers MAE below 50 meV/atom.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the chosen MLIP, regularization, and how well latent-feature corrections preserve relative phase stability across chemistries.
paper_title: Correcting DFT formation energies towards experimental accuracy using foundational MLIPs and latent-feature delta-learning
